Job Description

This Laboratory Technician role focuses on providing analytical support for gas and hydrocarbon liquid testing while strictly adhering to established quality, safety, environmental, and laboratory procedures. The position involves hands-on work with advanced analytical instruments, standardized test methods, and laboratory information systems to ensure accurate, timely, and well-documented results for internal and external stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Receive and log samples accurately into the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS).
Perform analytical testing on gas and hydrocarbon liquid samples using Gas Chromatography (GC), RVP, molecular weight, density, and distillation methods.
Follow standardized testing methods, including SOPs, GPA methods, and other approved analytical protocols to ensure data integrity and consistency.
Generate, review, and report test results to customers, and communicate findings clearly via phone and email as needed.
Conduct routine maintenance and basic troubleshooting of laboratory instruments and equipment to maintain optimal performance.
Assist with cylinder cleaning, preparation, and shipping to support laboratory operations and sample handling workflows.
Perform general laboratory housekeeping to maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area.
Follow all laboratory safety, quality, environmental, and ethics procedures at all times.
Maintain thorough documentation and recordkeeping for all tests, results, and laboratory activities in accordance with quality management system (QMS) requirements.

Essential Skills

Associates or Bachelors degree in Chemistry, Biology, Physical Science, or a closely related field.
Minimum of 2 years of laboratory experience in an analytical or testing environment.
Experience working with Gas Chromatography (GC) in a laboratory setting.
Proven ability to follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) and standardized test methods.
Strong documentation and recordkeeping skills, including accurate data entry into LIMS and other systems.
Ability to work comfortably and efficiently in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
Experience performing analytical testing such as RVP, molecular weight, density, and distillation.
Familiarity with quality management systems (QMS) and adherence to laboratory quality standards.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Experience in hydrocarbon, petroleum, chemical, energy, environmental, or testing laboratory settings.
Experience using LIMS systems for sample tracking and data management.
Familiarity with GPA and other industry-standard gas and hydrocarbon testing methods.
Background in life science or analytical testing disciplines.
Hands-on experience with laboratory instrumentation and basic equipment troubleshooting.
Attention to detail and strong organizational skills to manage multiple samples and tests.
Clear written and verbal communication skills for reporting and discussing test results.
Commitment to ethical laboratory practices and continuous improvement in safety and quality.

Work Environment

The role is based in an active laboratory environment where employees regularly work near moving mechanical parts and with materials that may be explosive, toxic, caustic, or otherwise hazardous. The position involves routine exposure to fumes, airborne particles, chemicals, and potential risks of electrical shock, with robust safety procedures and protective measures in place. Work is hands-on with analytical instruments such as Gas Chromatography systems and other testing equipment, supported by LIMS and quality management tools. Reasonable accommodations are available to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The culture emphasizes fair and competitive compensation, comprehensive health and wellness benefits, and a strong focus on safety, quality, and ethical conduct in all laboratory activities. Typical attire includes appropriate laboratory clothing and the use of required personal protective equipment to ensure safe operation in the lab.

This is a Contract position based out of Torrance, CA.

Pay And Benefits

Job Title: Quality Control Technician II
Job Description

The Quality Control Technician II plays a key role in ensuring that food products consistently meet internal quality expectations and regulatory food safety standards. This position focuses on routine monitoring, inspections, and data collection across production lines, helping to maintain a safe and compliant operation while supporting continuous improvement in quality assurance and quality control.

Responsibilities

Perform product temperature checks throughout production to verify compliance with food safety and quality specifications.
Conduct ATP equipment hygiene checks to confirm proper sanitation and cleanliness of production equipment.
Inspect equipment for cleanliness and sanitation readiness before and during use.
Perform Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspections on the production floor to ensure adherence to established standards.
Conduct sanitizer concentration verification to confirm proper dosing and effectiveness.
Measure pH and salt concentrations to ensure products meet defined quality parameters.
Perform detailed pre-operational inspections prior to production start-up to verify that all equipment and areas are ready for use.
Verify water temperatures used in production and sanitation processes to ensure compliance with established requirements.
Accurately document all inspection and test results in the appropriate systems or logs.
Report any deviations, non-conformances, or potential food safety risks promptly to quality assurance leadership.
Support running production lines after inspections are completed and cleared for operation.
Assist with basic calibration checks related to temperature, weight, and other critical control measurements as needed.
Follow established quality assurance and quality control procedures and contribute to maintaining a culture of food safety and continuous improvement.

Essential Skills

Hands-on experience in the meat industry, with familiarity with production processes and food safety considerations.
Strong understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and the ability to perform GMP inspections.
Experience performing temperature checks on products and process equipment in a production environment.
Ability to conduct weight checks and basic calibration-related activities for production and quality equipment.
Experience in quality assurance and quality control within a food manufacturing setting.
Ability to perform and interpret pH readings and salt concentration measurements.
Proficiency with basic computer skills for data entry, documentation, and reporting of quality results.
High level of attention to detail and accuracy when recording data and identifying deviations.
Comfort working in both hot and cold environments, including refrigerated and freezer areas.
Ability to work flexible shifts, including early morning or daytime schedules, as assigned.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Bachelors degree in Food Science or a related field is helpful and considered an asset.
Experience in both Quality Control Technician I and II level responsibilities is beneficial.
Ability to adapt to changing schedules and assignments across different production lines.
Strong communication skills to effectively report findings and collaborate with quality assurance leadership and production teams.
Demonstrated reliability and commitment to maintaining high standards of food safety and product quality.
Interest in long-term growth opportunities within a quality and food safety career path.

Work Environment

This role is based in a food manufacturing facility that operates across a range of temperatures, including hot production areas and cold environments such as refrigerated and freezer rooms, with conditions ranging approximately from below 0°F up to around 85°F. The position involves working on and around active production lines, conducting inspections before operations begin, and supporting line runs after equipment and areas are cleared. Standard safety and food manufacturing attire are required, which may include protective clothing suitable for both hot and cold conditions, along with appropriate personal protective equipment. Work schedules are flexible, with typical shifts such as 3:00 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. or 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the ability to adjust as operational needs change. The environment supports long-term career growth opportunities following an initial contract period, with exposure to a structured quality assurance and quality control culture focused on continuous improvement and regulatory compliance.

Associates or Bachelors degree in Chemistry, Biology, Physical Science, or a closely related field.

Experience working with Gas Chromatography (GC) in a laboratory setting.
Proven ability to follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) and standardized test methods.
Strong documentation and recordkeeping skills, including accurate data entry into LIMS and other systems.
Ability to work comfortably and efficiently in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
Experience performing analytical testing such as RVP, molecular weight, density, and distillation.

Experience in hydrocarbon, petroleum, chemical, energy, environmental, or testing laboratory settings.

Mechanical Engineering AI Trainer

Role Overview

Engagement: Fully remote, project-based AI training work

Hours: At least ~10h/week, no weekly maximum; full-time hours are available

Pay: $40-$125 per hour USD, paid via PayPal

Location: United States, Canada, or the UK

First step: Skills assessment: about 2-4 hours, unpaid

About the Role

A leading AI Lab is looking for experienced mechanical engineers to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real engineering work: sizing a component against a real load case, reading a CAD assembly and spotting what interferes at full travel, a tolerance stack up, a thermal or fluids calculation, a DFM decision, a failure analysis.

The models can already talk fluently about mechanical engineering; what they cannot yet do reliably is the actual work. You bring the judgment you have built catching the failure mode the spec sheet does not mention. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.
In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a component sizing calculation with a worked solution, a tolerance stack up, a CAD assembly review with interference and clearance findings, a thermal or fluids analysis, a DFM and DFA review, a failure analysis report, or a test and validation plan, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional mechanical engineering role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long form and self directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Responsibilities

Design challenging, realistic mechanical engineering tasks drawn from your own day to day work: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files an engineer would need (drawings, CAD models, load cases, material data, test data, specifications), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the calculation, design review, analysis or report) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write closed ended problems with worked solutions and acceptance criteria, and detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain, such as the right loads and factors, the right material, the right tolerances and the right failure modes considered, and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: wrong boundary conditions, unit errors, interferences missed, tolerance stacks that do not close, unsafe factors of safety, fabricated or ignored source files, and off brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across design, analysis, manufacturing and test, and review and refine tasks built by other engineers.

Domain Qualifications

2+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience preferred. Any specialty: design and product development, manufacturing, thermal, structural, automotive, aerospace, HVAC, robotics, energy, medical devices.
In progress Bachelor’s degree or higher in mechanical engineering or a related field. PE licensure is a plus but not required.
Depth in at least one of: mechanical design and CAD (geometry, clearances, tolerances, mechanisms); structures and materials (stress, deflection, fatigue, buckling, material selection, failure analysis); thermal and fluids (heat transfer, thermodynamics, HVAC, pumps and piping); dynamics and controls (vibration, kinematics, rotating machinery); manufacturing (DFM and DFA, process selection, GD&T, tolerance stack ups, cost and quality trade offs).
Fluency in the tools of your specialty: CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape, Creo, NX, CATIA or Inventor), FEA or CFD, or MATLAB or Python for engineering analysis.
Strong fundamentals across mechanics of materials, dynamics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics and manufacturing processes.
Meticulous: you check your own work and enjoy finding the edge case that breaks an assumption.

General Requirements

2+ years of hands on experience in your field preferred (see Domain qualifications above). Candidates with less experience are considered where the practical work is real.
Able to draw on your own real world experience and day to day workflows to craft scenarios that test whether an AI system can actually do the work.
Hands on practitioner: you currently do (or recently did) the work yourself at an individual contributor level, not solely in a managerial capacity.
Full professional or native level written and spoken English, with strong written communication. You can explain complex professional reasoning clearly and concisely, and articulate why a result is wrong, not only that it is.
Comfort with ambiguity and attention to detail. You can orient in a new set of files and build an accurate, deep working picture of it quickly, especially when the subject sits partly outside your own specialization. You verify what a document claims against the underlying numbers, sources or facts.
Capable of interpreting feedback, judging which parts of it are actually correct, and applying it without hand holding. When stuck, you look for the answer rather than waiting for one.
Ability to ramp quickly on unfamiliar work from written material and instructions alone, including where that material is incomplete (for example, writing grading rubrics for the first time).
General familiarity with AI and LLM tools. You have used models like Claude or ChatGPT in professional work and have the judgment to tell a well reasoned answer from a plausible sounding but incorrect one.
Baseline tech literacy: comfortable with cloud file tools (e.g., Google Workspace), managing browser profiles, downloading and installing desktop apps (e.g., Claude), and everyday file handling (e.g., converting between Excel and Google Sheets, zipping files for sharing).
Available at least 10 hours per week, with no weekly maximum. Consistent availability is valued and full time hours are available.
Based in the United States, Canada, or the UK.

Compensation and Terms

Pay: $40-$125/hr USD. Paid via PayPal on a regular cadence.
Contract position. Fully remote. Minimum 10 hours per week with no weekly maximum.
Flexible scheduling. Multi day task timers let you spread work across days.
Access to Claude and ChatGPT is provided through the project; no personal subscription is required.

What to Expect

Apply through your agency link and create your account.
Complete the skills assessment (about 2 to 4 hours, unpaid). It tests domain fit, careful reading, and how you judge a model's output against a professional standard. All work must be your own; submissions produced with AI tools are rejected, and this is the single most common reason candidates do not pass.
Our team reviews your assessment. If you pass, you complete onboarding, start on regular paid projects in your field, and complete a short training project that walks through how tasks, files, and rubrics are built.
Propose a task from your professional experience: the scenario, the prompt, the files you will build, and where you expect the model to fail. An expert reviewer reads it and sends written feedback either way.
Once your proposal is accepted, build the task in full and run it against frontier models. Every completed task goes through expert review, and experienced contributors are invited to review and refine other experts' tasks.
Each stage is a gate: work must be accepted before you move on. You are compensated for every step you complete, but not every submission is accepted. Feedback and revision are a normal part of the process. Support is available through platform instructions, onboarding materials, a dedicated Slack channel, and office hours.

Job Description

This Laboratory Technician role focuses on providing analytical support for gas and hydrocarbon liquid testing while strictly adhering to established quality, safety, environmental, and laboratory procedures. Responsibilities

Receive and log samples accurately into the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS).
Perform analytical testing on gas and hydrocarbon liquid samples using Gas Chromatography (GC), RVP, molecular weight, density, and distillation methods.
Follow standardized testing methods, including SOPs, GPA methods, and other approved analytical protocols to ensure data integrity and consistency.
Generate, review, and report test results to customers, and communicate findings clearly via phone and email as needed.
Conduct routine maintenance and basic troubleshooting of laboratory instruments and equipment to maintain optimal performance.

Maintain thorough documentation and recordkeeping for all tests, results, and laboratory activities in accordance with quality management system (QMS) requirements.

Essential Skills

Associates or Bachelors degree in Chemistry, Biology, Physical Science, or a closely related field.
Minimum of 2 years of laboratory experience in an analytical or testing environment.
Experience working with Gas Chromatography (GC) in a laboratory setting.
Proven ability to follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) and standardized test methods.
Strong documentation and recordkeeping skills, including accurate data entry into LIMS and other systems.
Ability to work comfortably and efficiently in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
Experience performing analytical testing such as RVP, molecular weight, density, and distillation.

Experience in hydrocarbon, petroleum, chemical, energy, environmental, or testing laboratory settings.

Mechanical Engineering AI Trainer

Role Overview

Engagement: Fully remote, project-based AI training work

Hours: At least ~10h/week, no weekly maximum; full-time hours are available

About the Role

A leading AI Lab is looking for experienced mechanical engineers to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real engineering work: sizing a component against a real load case, reading a CAD assembly and spotting what interferes at full travel, a tolerance stack up, a thermal or fluids calculation, a DFM decision, a failure analysis.

The models can already talk fluently about mechanical engineering; what they cannot yet do reliably is the actual work. You bring the judgment you have built catching the failure mode the spec sheet does not mention. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.
In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a component sizing calculation with a worked solution, a tolerance stack up, a CAD assembly review with interference and clearance findings, a thermal or fluids analysis, a DFM and DFA review, a failure analysis report, or a test and validation plan, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional mechanical engineering role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long form and self directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Responsibilities

Design challenging, realistic mechanical engineering tasks drawn from your own day to day work: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files an engineer would need (drawings, CAD models, load cases, material data, test data, specifications), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the calculation, design review, analysis or report) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write closed ended problems with worked solutions and acceptance criteria, and detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain, such as the right loads and factors, the right material, the right tolerances and the right failure modes considered, and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: wrong boundary conditions, unit errors, interferences missed, tolerance stacks that do not close, unsafe factors of safety, fabricated or ignored source files, and off brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across design, analysis, manufacturing and test, and review and refine tasks built by other engineers.

Domain Qualifications

2+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience preferred. Any specialty: design and product development, manufacturing, thermal, structural, automotive, aerospace, HVAC, robotics, energy, medical devices.
In progress Bachelor’s degree or higher in mechanical engineering or a related field. PE licensure is a plus but not required.
Depth in at least one of: mechanical design and CAD (geometry, clearances, tolerances, mechanisms); structures and materials (stress, deflection, fatigue, buckling, material selection, failure analysis); thermal and fluids (heat transfer, thermodynamics, HVAC, pumps and piping); dynamics and controls (vibration, kinematics, rotating machinery); manufacturing (DFM and DFA, process selection, GD&T, tolerance stack ups, cost and quality trade offs).
Fluency in the tools of your specialty: CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape, Creo, NX, CATIA or Inventor), FEA or CFD, or MATLAB or Python for engineering analysis.
Strong fundamentals across mechanics of materials, dynamics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics and manufacturing processes.
Meticulous: you check your own work and enjoy finding the edge case that breaks an assumption.

General Requirements

2+ years of hands on experience in your field preferred (see Domain qualifications above). Candidates with less experience are considered where the practical work is real.
Able to draw on your own real world experience and day to day workflows to craft scenarios that test whether an AI system can actually do the work.
Hands on practitioner: you currently do (or recently did) the work yourself at an individual contributor level, not solely in a managerial capacity.
Full professional or native level written and spoken English, with strong written communication. You can explain complex professional reasoning clearly and concisely, and articulate why a result is wrong, not only that it is.
Comfort with ambiguity and attention to detail. You can orient in a new set of files and build an accurate, deep working picture of it quickly, especially when the subject sits partly outside your own specialization. You verify what a document claims against the underlying numbers, sources or facts.
Capable of interpreting feedback, judging which parts of it are actually correct, and applying it without hand holding. When stuck, you look for the answer rather than waiting for one.
Ability to ramp quickly on unfamiliar work from written material and instructions alone, including where that material is incomplete (for example, writing grading rubrics for the first time).
General familiarity with AI and LLM tools. You have used models like Claude or ChatGPT in professional work and have the judgment to tell a well reasoned answer from a plausible sounding but incorrect one.
Baseline tech literacy: comfortable with cloud file tools (e.g., Google Workspace), managing browser profiles, downloading and installing desktop apps (e.g., Claude), and everyday file handling (e.g., converting between Excel and Google Sheets, zipping files for sharing).
Available at least 10 hours per week, with no weekly maximum. Consistent availability is valued and full time hours are available.
Based in the United States, Canada, or the UK.

Compensation and Terms

Pay: $40-$125/hr USD. Paid via PayPal on a regular cadence.
Contract position. Fully remote. Minimum 10 hours per week with no weekly maximum.
Flexible scheduling. Multi day task timers let you spread work across days.
Access to Claude and ChatGPT is provided through the project; no personal subscription is required.

What to Expect

Apply through your agency link and create your account.
Complete the skills assessment (about 2 to 4 hours, unpaid). It tests domain fit, careful reading, and how you judge a model's output against a professional standard. All work must be your own; submissions produced with AI tools are rejected, and this is the single most common reason candidates do not pass.
Our team reviews your assessment. If you pass, you complete onboarding, start on regular paid projects in your field, and complete a short training project that walks through how tasks, files, and rubrics are built.
Propose a task from your professional experience: the scenario, the prompt, the files you will build, and where you expect the model to fail. An expert reviewer reads it and sends written feedback either way.
Once your proposal is accepted, build the task in full and run it against frontier models. Every completed task goes through expert review, and experienced contributors are invited to review and refine other experts' tasks.
Each stage is a gate: work must be accepted before you move on. You are compensated for every step you complete, but not every submission is accepted. Feedback and revision are a normal part of the process. Support is available through platform instructions, onboarding materials, a dedicated Slack channel, and office hours.
